_meta.description: Crypto addresses on sanctions and seizure lists published by governments other than the U.S., and wallets U.S. courts have ordered forfeited. A match means the funds touched a wallet a government has frozen, seized or forfeited.
_meta.provenance: UK: https://sanctionslist.fcdo.gov.uk/docs/UK-Sanctions-List.csv. EU: https://webgate.ec.europa.eu/fsd/fsf/public/files/xmlFullSanctionsList_1_1/content?token=dG9rZW4tMjAxNw. Israel (NBCTF), Japan (MOF) and France (DG Tresor) via OpenSanctions, which extracts them from each publisher's own documents; OpenSanctions data is licensed CC BY-NC 4.0. U.S. forfeiture orders: DOJ official notifications (forfeiture.gov), as held in data/us_forfeiture_orders.json. Built by backend/scripts/import_intl_sanctions.py.
_meta.verification_note: Each entry is copied from a government publication and names every authority that lists it. It establishes that the government froze or seized the address as of the review date; it does NOT establish that a counterparty who received funds from it is culpable, nor that the measure has force in Indian law. Only measures still in force are included.
_meta.schema: labels maps an address to {category, entity, label, source, authorities}, plus valid_until (the last day it is in force) when every listing behind it has an end date; category is seized when only seizure orders name it, sanctioned otherwise

il_mod_crypto.note: Israel listings re-screened offline against this version; every listing whose measures had all ended was removed. Other authorities' listings were not re-read, so last_reviewed is unchanged.

us_forfeiture.note: Added offline from this source without re-reading the other lists, so last_reviewed is unchanged.
